text: How should SkyHarbor decide between predictive maintenance AI and crew recovery AI?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
7 hours) come from stacking predictive maintenance AND crew-ops AI together, not choosing one. That said, if funding forces a sequence, lead with predictive maintenance and follow with crew recovery within the same fiscal window. Here's the reasoning. Predictive maintenance is the upstream lever — it prevents the disruption from happening.
The loaded MRO predictive maintenance capability is flagged early-stage AI maturity but critical business criticality, which means the substrate exists but the model work is ahead of you. Crew Recovery is downstream — it optimizes how you respond once a disruption hits. IROPS recovery decisioning is also early-stage.
Both need work, but maintenance failures are a primary driver of the crew disruptions Crew Recovery would then untangle, so fixing the upstream cause reduces the downstream load.
The Airline Demo-specific tiebreakers: Data readiness — Maintenance Delay Feed and Aircraft Tail Assignment are loaded as critical assets, but Crew Legality Feed and Crew Availability Feed carry heavier regulatory weight (DOT duty-time rules, union constraints). Crew Recovery cannot go autonomous until crew legality freshness SLA is owner-certified. Predictive maintenance has a lighter control surface.
Model risk — Crew Recovery touches humans directly (duty assignments, legality). It needs model-risk tier approval, human-in-loop workflow, and override logs before it scales. Predictive maintenance decisions route through existing MRO signoff chains, which is a shorter governance path.
